### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **129** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/package.json`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**49** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33043bd8a2b34ed2efdc188f38173c1c44ca3f36`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/package.json`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectstack.config.ts (literal, 38 pages)`
- **74** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33043bd8a2b34ed2efdc188f38173c1c44ca3f36` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `41fa412d8f583717d5bec7badeb02bcb76e16a1f` — the merge of head `30360bf2c66a057d02fe1e8dee157d425953f7e6` into base `33043bd8a2b34ed2efdc188f38173c1c44ca3f36`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 41fa412d8f583717d5bec7badeb02bcb76e16a1f && git checkout 41fa412d8f583717d5bec7badeb02bcb76e16a1f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 33043bd8a2b34ed2efdc188f38173c1c44ca3f36 30360bf2c66a057d02fe1e8dee157d425953f7e6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 33043bd8a2b34ed2efdc188f38173c1c44ca3f36 && git merge --no-ff 30360bf2c66a057d02fe1e8dee157d425953f7e6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33043bd8a2b34ed2efdc188f38173c1c44ca3f36
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 33043bd8a2b34ed2efdc188f38173c1c44ca3f36` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c78ea5a418693a925b325a8ab492d4d175608ad0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/cli.ts, exporter.ts, generic.ts, index.ts, manifest.ts, pass.ts, record.ts, screenshots.ts, source.ts, transcript.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/orchestrate.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/cli.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, packages/qa/scenarios/test/export/exporter.test.ts, fixture.ts, screenshots.test.ts + packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/scorecard.ts, project.ts, app.ts, driver.ts, namespace.ts, prompts.ts (read, not reviewed), objectstack-ai/gallery AGENTS.md, README.md, apps/README.md (the rules the output is held to). `reviewFace` returns no `hits` on this file list (no published schema, no governed path, `Clause-②: no` without an arm); the brief orders the contract tier, so the whole diff is in scope.

Inputs: card #30349 body and all 10 comments (the claim 6683477231 and the two dev reports read as claims), follow-up #30932, PR #30930 body, labels and file list, the net diff `origin/main...c78ea5a4` (merge-base 1697d5ca; 17 files, +2226/−37), the files read at the head, the gallery clone at 09ce9b0, and the 68 check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

**Gallery rule 1 — only scenarios that passed every half.** `pass.ts` `judgeRecord`: the newest record per card (`record.ts` `readRunRecords`, `date` compared as ISO text, file-name order breaks a tie) is read from its `results` rows, nothing re-scored. Scratch mode is required and owes six halves; template mode, when the record holds it, owes its three iterate halves; a verdict other than `pass` (so `not-run`, `partial`, `fail`, `blocked`) and a missing row are each a reason; a skipped template mode fails on its `not-run` rows. Then every Run half the record holds is walked and each question or operation carrying `notMeasured` is a reason of its own, so a half that reads `pass` over a refused seed row does not pass (the scorecard's `askTally`/`opsTally` leave such turns out of both counts — confirmed in `scorecard.ts`). An errored turn counts in total and not in passed, so it cannot pass either. Held. Pinned by 5 `judgeRecord` tests on a real `runCard` run, including the ct4 refused-seed case that keeps every verdict `pass` and still refuses.

**Gallery rule 2 — nothing customer-derived.** `generic.ts` `NO_GENERIC_MARKER` refuses every card; `exporter.ts` 159 `opts.isGeneric ?? NO_GENERIC_MARKER`; `cli.ts` never sets `isGeneric`, `parseExportArgs` throws on any unknown flag (tested with `--generic`), `ExportCliDeps` carries only `screenshots`, and no `process.env` read anywhere in `src/export/` touches the guard (the only env read is `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` for the Chromium path). No bypass outside tests. The `exportGallery` parameter is the test seam, in a private package. Held.

**Gallery rule 3 — no secret, no local path.** Persona API keys never reach the record (`runHalf` strips `apiKey`); the recording stores `ParsedTurn`s only, never the `mcp.apiKey`; `Recording.files` (authoring sources) is not exported. `redactWorkDir` replaces every occurrence of the work directory in `run-record.json`, `scorecard.json` and `transcript.json`. **MUST-FIX M1:** the replacement is incomplete when `--work DIR` is given. `exporter.ts` 233 sets `workDir = opts.workDir ?? record.evidenceDir` and 240/250/270 redact with that value alone, but the record's strings — `evidenceDir` itself, every build command `tail` (`ran in ...`, the fixture shows the shape), any `error` text — carry the ORIGINAL machine's `evidenceDir`. With `--work` (whose own doc is "records moved off the machine that ran them") that absolute path of another machine is written verbatim into all three JSON files. The test `not.toContain(fx.work)` runs only without `workDir`. Fix: redact `record.evidenceDir` and `opts.workDir` both, and pin it under `workDir`. (Also noted, not blocking: `v.split(workDir)` has no path boundary, so a short work dir such as `/tmp` rewrites `/tmpfoo`; and an absolute path outside the work dir in a command tail is not redacted — unlikely on a passing build.)

**Gallery rule 3 — the `source/` list.** `source.ts` is an allow-list: `objectstack.config.ts` (required), `objectstack.manifest.json`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, and the `src/` tree, regular files only, `node_modules`/`dist`/`.objectstack`/`.git` never, a symbolic link anywhere refuses. `.env`, `.agents`, `.claude`, `README.md`, `Dockerfile` are outside the list; the fixture plants each and the layout test asserts the 12-file tree. Held.

**② The transcript.** `transcript.ts` `buildTranscript`: for every graded question turn the recording is looked up by `stepKey` (card/mode/phase/step/persona — the same key the `RecordingDriver` wrote), a missing turn refuses, and the recorded reply is re-graded with `gradeCardAnswer` under the same inputs the runner used (namespaced scenario, `hiddenValues` for the persona, `citationLabels(original)` — compared against `runHalf` 455-460, identical), a canonical-JSON mismatch refuses. `mergeRecordings` refuses a key recorded twice with different turns. Fail-closed: a missing recording refuses (test), a partial one refuses on the first graded turn without a reply, a turn with `error` or `notMeasured` has no grade check but such a record never passes rule 1, so it is never exported. Sound.

**③ Re-export.** Each app is written whole to `apps/.staging-ID`, then `rmSync(apps/ID)` and `renameSync` (exporter.ts 186-188); a refused app's staging is removed. Previous `index.json` is parsed with the strict schema BEFORE anything is touched and an invalid one throws (test: tree unchanged). Every app the previous index listed that did not export this time is deleted and leaves the index with its reason; a directory the index never listed is left alone and named in `unowned` (`isDirectory()` filter, so the gallery's hand-written `apps/README.md` survives). A stale or hand-made directory with an exporting card's id is overwritten by the swap — the exporter owns `apps/ID` for the ids it exports, acceptable. `index.json`: `serializeIndex` sorts by id, parses through `GalleryIndexSchema` (strictObject at every level, refine: sorted and unique ids, `path` equals `apps/ID`, screenshots under it), no timestamp, written only when the bytes differ (tested byte-stable, file for file). **SHOULD-FIX S3:** an app leaves the gallery whenever the runs directory holds no record of it (199-203), so an empty or wrong `--runs` deletes every app and the index entries with exit 0 — consider refusing when the previous index is non-empty and the runs directory holds zero scenario records.

**④ Screenshots.** `captureScreenshots` boots with the runner's `bootDev` and `HttpApp` (wired in `cli.ts` 97), signs in as `ADMIN`, seeds with `seedApp(namespacedScenario(scenario), app, [])` — the runner's loop on the runner's namespaced card — then shoots, closes the browser and stops the app in `finally`. The seed-loop move (`orchestrate.ts` 386-414 vs main 379-406) is textually the same loop with `seed` for `half.seed`; `modeDir` yields the same two directory names main spelled inline. **SHOULD-FIX S2:** one behaviour difference in the exception path: on main `half.seed` was mutated in place, so an `insertRow` throw left the partial `inserted`/`refused` tally in the record next to `half.error`; now `half.seed = await seedApp(...)` never assigns and the record shows `inserted: 0, refused: []`. Verdicts are unchanged (the half is `not-run` or `blocked` either way); the scorecard's seed cell is not. The 18.3 currency-dialog handling (`screenshots.ts` 254-263) visits the first shot's page once unshot, then every shot is still taken and existence-checked; a `goto` error propagates, so it hides no failure. **SHOULD-FIX S1:** `page.goto` does not throw on a non-2xx response, and nothing reads the response or the page, so a Console not-found or error view is shot and exported as proof; read `(await page.goto(...))?.ok()` and refuse the shot otherwise. A skipped shot is reported in `ScreenshotResult.skipped`, the CLI summary, the README (`no KIND screenshot: REASON`) and is absent from the index — never silent. A step that throws refuses the app and, if it was listed before, removes it (fail closed, as designed). **SHOULD-FIX S4:** `--no-screenshots` yields an index entry with `screenshots: []` indistinguishable from a real export; the gallery's proof set includes screenshots, so the summary should say loudly that the output is not publishable, or the flag should refuse to replace an entry that had shots.

**⑤ The landing.** `Part of #30349` is honest: the write path, the first real export and the marker (#30932) remain on the card; `check-partof-closing-keyword` and the PR-body guards are green. `skip-changeset` is right: `@objectstack/scenarios` is `"private": true`, the diff publishes nothing from a released package. `playwright-core` `1.63.0`: the exact pin `packages/qa/dogfood` and `packages/services/service-print` already hold; the lockfile diff is 3 added lines in the `packages/qa/scenarios` importer, the `playwright-core@1.63.0` package and snapshot entries pre-exist, no new transitive package. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` match a tree that touches no `packages/spec` file. The diff touches none of `loader.ts`, `schema.ts`, `docs/qa/scenarios/*.json`, the package README or `refusals.test.ts` (verified against the file list and the tree), no `.github/**`, no changeset. No write path to the gallery: `src/export/` has no `child_process`, `fetch`, git or GitHub call; the only spawn is the runner's `bootDev`; writes go under `--out` only. PR body vs tree: the 24 + 12 test counts, the layout, the allow-list, the refusal order, the `$WORK` claim (true only without `--work`, see M1), the runner touch-ups and the lockfile description all match the tree.

**Check-runs on c78ea5a4:** 68 runs, all `completed`, none in progress; conclusions `success` or `skipped` (Check Changeset skipped by the label; Dogfood opt-in shards, Temporal, UI Published Artifacts, 18.x harness, packed-tarball skipped by their filters), none `failure`. Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 8/8, Test UI 16/16, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Validate Package Dependencies, PR-body guards: success.

### ② Semver level

None owed. `@objectstack/scenarios` is private and unpublished; no released package moves. `skip-changeset` is the correct label. Nothing an author can write changes: `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No governed surface in the file list; no workflow; no spec, loader, schema or card change; no release act.
- New third-party runtime dependency in a private QA package (`playwright-core` 1.63.0, already in the lockfile twice); no new package in the lockfile.
- Local side effects only: the exporter spawns `objectstack dev --fresh` on the run's scratch project and launches headless Chromium when screenshots are on; it writes under `--out` and nowhere else.
- The CLI exits 0 whatever it refused (refusals go to stderr); a pipeline cannot read "nothing exported" off the exit code. Noted, not a finding.
- Recording text (model replies and tool outputs) is written to the gallery as the transcript; it is seed-derived and synthetic by the gallery's own rule, and the re-grade proves the join.

### ④ Design judgment

Against the gallery's rules (AGENTS.md: exporter-only writes to `apps/**` and `index.json`, every half passed, generic only, no secrets; README: function, title, screenshots, question count, framework version, run date in the index), the module holds where it can and refuses where it cannot show compliance: the refuse-all guard is the right default while the card schema has no origin marker, `title.zh: null` is an honest gap tracked on #30932 rather than a sentence passed off as a title, and the hand-written `apps/README.md` is left to the maintainer as the gallery's AGENTS.md lists it. The staging-and-swap re-export, the strict pre-validated index and the proven transcript join are sound. The one place the rules are not held is the `--work` redaction gap (M1): the flag exists for records moved between machines, and in that exact case the other machine's absolute work directory is written into three gallery files. A one-line fix plus one test; everything else on this head stands.

**Must-fix**
- M1 — `exporter.ts` 233/240/250/270: with `--work DIR`, `record.evidenceDir` and every record string naming it are written unredacted into `run-record.json`, `scorecard.json`, `transcript.json`. Redact both the record's `evidenceDir` and `opts.workDir`; pin under `workDir`.

**Should-fix**
- S1 — `screenshots.ts` 245/262: a failed navigation (non-2xx, Console error view) is shot and exported; check the `goto` response and refuse.
- S2 — `orchestrate.ts` 437: the seed tally is lost from the record when `insertRow` throws mid-loop (main kept the partial counts); assign progressively or catch inside `seedApp`.
- S3 — `exporter.ts` 199-203: an empty or wrong `--runs` removes every listed app with exit 0; refuse when the previous index is non-empty and no scenario record was found.
- S4 — `--no-screenshots` output is indistinguishable from a real export in `index.json`; mark it in the summary or refuse to replace an entry that had shots.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-30349-gallery-exporter`
Reviewed-by: `session_017ihL2ebbZkr2QAEG1x7UC8`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `30360bf2c66a057d02fe1e8dee157d425953f7e6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: delta `c78ea5a418..30360bf2c6` (one commit, 8 files, +317/−34, all under packages/qa/scenarios): src/export/cli.ts, exporter.ts, record.ts, screenshots.ts, src/runner/orchestrate.ts, test/export/exporter.test.ts, test/export/screenshots.test.ts, test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts + the live PR body, the dev's delta report 6685891798 (read as claims), the FAIL record 6685278277 this delta answers, and the Console source at the released tag `@objectstack/console@18.3.0` (commit 83d7e4ae) and on main (read to judge the not-found markers). Nothing outside the package moved: `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, loader, schema, cards, README, workflows untouched in the delta. The round-2 record's judgments on the rest of the tree stand; this record re-judges what the delta changed.

### ① Derived judgments

**M1 — `$WORK` redaction, was must-fix. Fixed.** `exporter.ts` `workDirsOf(record.evidenceDir, opts.workDir)` yields the record's `evidenceDir`, `--work` when given, and `realpathSync` of each that exists on this machine (a missing one is skipped silently, which is the moved-record case). `exportOne` builds one `redact` over that set and applies it to the transcript (so `transcript.json` and `transcript.md`), the scorecard (so `scorecard.json` and `scorecard.md`), `run-record.json` (`rf.raw`) and now `README.md`; `source/` is copied as written, which is right (authored files, not record text). `record.ts` `redactWorkDir` takes one or many directories, strips trailing slashes, drops `/` and the empty string, sorts longest first, escapes for the regex and matches only at a path-name boundary: not after `[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]`, not before `[A-Za-z0-9_~-]` or a `.` that starts a suffix; a following `/` is allowed, so `/w/x` under `/w` becomes `$WORK/x`, and `$$WORK` in `String.replace` is the literal `$WORK`. Whole-name matching holds (`/tmp` leaves `/tmpfoo`, `/tmp.d/x`, `/var/tmp/y`, `x/tmp`), nested directories replace longest first.
Test: `exporter.test.ts` rewrites a real `runCrm` record so every string naming its work directory names `/srv/ci-runner-7/scenario-work`, asserts the build tails name it too, exports with `workDir` set to the real project directory, then reads every file under `--out` and asserts none contains the other machine's path, `workDir` or its real path, and that `evidenceDir` reads `$WORK`; a second test pins the boundary rules and the nested and `/`-skip cases. This test fails against the round-2 code (only `--work` redacted; the other path survives). Note, not a finding: it does not fail if only `evidenceDir` were redacted, because no output string derives from `--work` (the project path is read, never written), so the `--work` and realpath redaction is defence in depth rather than a pinned failure mode; and a path written in `file:///...` form is preceded by `/`, so the boundary leaves it (no record field produces that form today). Complete for every file the exporter writes.

**S1 — failed pages, was should-fix. Fixed, and the markers hold on the released Console.** `playwrightBrowser.visit` now returns a `PageReading` (the navigation response status or `null`, and which of `CONSOLE_NOT_FOUND`'s test ids or titles the page draws); `pageRefusal` refuses no response, any status outside 2xx other than 304, then any not-found view; `capture` returns `shown: true` or `shown: false, reason`, and `captureScreenshots` removes the file, drops the shot and records a skipped shot with the Console path and reason. The existence check for a shown shot remains. 304 as loaded is sound: each shot's page is visited twice (the warm-up), so the second navigation can legitimately revalidate the document; a 304 is the browser rendering the document it holds, not a missing page, and a client-side not-found is caught by the marker check that runs regardless of status. The four test ids (`object-not-found`, `object-package-disabled` in `objectViewChrome.tsx`, `record-page-not-found` in `RecordDetailView.tsx`, `form-not-found` in `FormPage.tsx`) and the router catch-all `console.notFound.title` with default `Page not found` in `AppContent.tsx` all exist at tag `@objectstack/console@18.3.0` (83d7e4ae), the released Console the screenshots run against, as well as on main. The title is the one text-matched marker and is localised (zh: `页面不存在`); the browser context is `locale: 'en-US'` and the Console's `pickInitialLanguage` reads `navigator.language`, so the English title is what renders. Not a should-fix; a hardening note: adding the zh title (or a test id on `RouteNotFound` upstream) would make that one marker locale-independent.
Tests: `pageRefusal` on 200/204/304, null, 301/401/403/404/500/502 and a not-found view; the marker list pinned; `captureScreenshots` with a double answering 500 for the list page and `record-page-not-found` for the record page: both skipped with their reasons, both files gone, the dashboard kept, close then stop. Pinned.

**S2 — seed tally on a throw, was should-fix. Fixed.** `seedApp` takes the tally to fill (`seed` parameter, default a fresh object per call) and `runHalf` passes `half.seed`, so an `insertRow` throw leaves `inserted`, `refused` and `handlesAsAdmin` as far as they got, next to `half.error`, as on main. The screenshot step's call (`seedApp(ns, app, [])`) keeps the default and the return value. Test: `orchestrate.test.ts` `ThrowingApp` refuses ac2 then throws on ct1; asserts `half.error`, `half.seed` equals 2 inserted, ac2 refused, `handlesAsAdmin: ['u_tia']`, no questions asked, scorecard seed 2/3 with 1 refused. Fails against the round-2 shape. Pinned.

**S3 — empty runs over a non-empty index, was should-fix. Fixed.** `exportGallery` throws before `apps/` is touched when `newest.size === 0` and the previous index lists apps, naming both; the CLI's top-level handler exits 1. Test: after an export, a runs directory holding only non-runner JSON rejects through `exportGallery` and through `main`, the tree byte-identical both times; with no previous index an empty runs directory still writes an empty index. Pinned. By design and acceptable: a runs directory that holds records for some cards but not a listed one still removes that one (the exporter owns what the index lists).

**S4 — `--no-screenshots` over an export that had shots, was should-fix. Fixed.** In `exportGallery`, when `screenshots === false`, the previous entry has shots and `apps/ID` exists, the fresh staging is discarded, the previous entry is pushed as-is, `summary.kept` names it with the reason, and `renderSummary` prints a `kept` line on stderr and counts it; an app whose newest record fails is still removed (the keep applies only after `exportOne` succeeded). Test: export with one shot, then `screenshots: false`: nothing exported or removed, `kept` names the app, index unchanged, tree byte-identical, both summary lines pinned; then a newer failing record removes it. Pinned. Consequence worth knowing, not a finding: the kept entry keeps the previous run's date and record even when a newer run passed.

**Anything else touched.** `cli.ts`: the summary gains the `kept` line and the stderr routing regex; the docblock gains the `--work` and `--no-screenshots` notes and the empty-runs paragraph — nit: that paragraph is inserted between `--no-screenshots` and `--chromium`, so the flag list is interrupted (prose only). No other behaviour changed; no file outside the package; `package.json` and the lockfile unchanged in the delta; still no write path to the gallery and no workflow.

**PR body vs tree.** The live body (head 30360bf2) describes round 3 in the maintainer brief, the `No local path` paragraph (both directories and their real paths, longest first, path-name boundary, six files, `source/` as written), `pageRefusal` with the four test ids and the title, the empty-runs refusal with non-zero exit, `kept`, and the seed tally; test counts 28 + 16 + one orchestrate test match the tree (28, 16, 14 `it` blocks). `Part of #30349`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `skip-changeset` unchanged and still right.

**Check-runs on 30360bf2:** every run `completed`, none in progress; conclusions `success` or `skipped` (Check Changeset by the label; Dogfood opt-in shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal, UI Published Artifacts, 18.x harness, packed-tarball, schedule gate by their filters; duplicate Auto Label and Check PR Size runs skipped by trigger); none `failure`.
